claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between thermodynamic and kinetic factors.
High configurational entropy is the relevant thermodynamic stabilizing factor in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Sluggish diffusion is the relevant kinetic factor controlling phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Thermal treatments spanning 600°C to 1200°C provide the proposed controlled comparison.
Local chemical order and phase-boundary configurations mediate thermally induced behavior in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Dynamic evolution of local chemical order and phase-boundary configurations changes phase stability and transformation behavior.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 will exhibit a ductile-brittle transition within a temperature-dependent regime.
The temperature of the predicted ductile-brittle transition depends on the balance between configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion.
The ductile-brittle transition is expected to occur within a bounded or narrow temperature window.
Failure to observe a ductile-brittle transition in the predicted temperature regime would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis specifically identifies high configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion as the governing mechanism, while the uncertainty field states that the specific mechanisms governing phase stability remain uncertain.
